This page is different from Rules: Rules only filter candidate entries, while Component cleanup really enables or disables Android components with Root. It manages launcher entries, tiles, create-shortcut entries, and widgets. Desired disabled state is persisted and reconciled after boot, unlock, and app updates.

Apps filters All, User apps or System apps and limits bulk targets. Lock or unlock app and component rows with the three-dot menu or a long-press; Locked under All aggregates category locks. Bulk actions skip locked items, and a locked child row cannot be selected directly until it is unlocked. A lock is not actual component disable. Protected system components remain read-only.

Checked means desired disabled; unchecked means desired enabled. Pending changes may differ from actual Android state. Root operations run only after Apply changes is confirmed at the bottom. List Cleaner then reads back the system state, saves the disabled policy and reconciles restored components after boot or app updates.

Individual selections and bulk actions first update a pending draft and do not immediately change Android. Confirm bulk targets, then confirm Apply changes at the bottom before Root operations run and the result is verified. Unlike Rules filtering, this changes real component state. Re-enabling does not restore previous launcher, tile or widget placement.

Uses Android subsystem registries where available: launcher activities, standard TileService entries, LauncherApps shortcut configuration activities plus legacy creation entries, and AppWidgetManager providers with manifest fallback. This never disables the entire app.

Lists exported ACTION_MAIN + CATEGORY_LAUNCHER activities and aliases. Disabling one removes that launcher entry and can make an app harder to open if it is the app’s only launcher activity; the app itself remains installed.
Only standard TileService components are listed. Built-in system tiles without an independent service, such as Wi-Fi or Bluetooth, are unsupported; core system components are display-only.

Lists LauncherApps shortcut configuration activities and legacy shortcut creation entries, not individual Manifest, Dynamic or Pinned ShortcutInfo. Long-press shortcut candidates belong under Rule cleanup and may come from runtime Hook observations or read-only proactive discovery. Disabling a configuration activity can affect other entry points.

Uses the AppWidgetManager provider registry first and merges manifest widget receivers as a fallback. Disabling can break placed widgets; enabling does not guarantee restoration of the previous layout.
